card.occupation: Student nurse (final year, MSc Adult Nursing pre-registration) currently on full-time hospital placement on an acute medical ward
card.education_detail: Went to a comprehensive in Bexleyheath and did A-levels in PE, Biology and Business. Took a BSc in Sport and Exercise Science at a university in Kent and got a 2:1. Worked three years as a healthcare assistant, then started a two-year graduate-entry MSc in Adult Nursing at a London university. Placements run 37.5-hour weeks of long days and nights, so she's a full-time student who works full-time hours.
card.household: Rents a one-bedroom flat above a dry cleaner's with her husband Dean, 31, a gas engineer. They married two years ago at a registry office with a pub do afterwards. No kids and no pets, though Dean keeps talking about getting a dog and she keeps saying no.
card.cultural_background: White British. Grew up in Bexleyheath with a mum who's a school receptionist, a dad who drives for a building supplies firm, and a younger brother. Not religious, and neither were her parents beyond weddings and funerals. A fairly typical outer-south-east-London upbringing: Saturday football, family holidays in Kent and Spain, Sunday roasts at Nan's.
card.professional_persona: Practical and quick on the ward, and good in a crisis because she doesn't overthink. She is blunt with colleagues and has been told more than once to soften how she says things. She will always own up to a mistake straight away and won't fudge a chart. Her paperwork is often late, and she leaves her reflective essays until the night before. Mentors rate her clinical hands-on care and nag her about documentation.
card.sports_persona: Played netball through school and university and still does Tuesday nights in a casual league when the rota allows. Watches Charlton with her dad and brother occasionally. She would rather play than watch, and the gym membership mostly goes unused.
card.arts_persona: Not really into it. Watches whatever's on: reality TV, Gogglebox, the odd crime drama Dean picks. She has no interest in galleries or theatre and says so. Listens to Capital or a playlist of the same 2010s pop she's had for years.
card.travel_persona: Likes the same things every time: a week all-inclusive in Tenerife or Majorca, sunbed, pool, done. They went to Lanzarote for the honeymoon. She finds city breaks tiring. Long-haul doesn't appeal and it isn't affordable on a student budget anyway.
card.culinary_persona: Plain eater. Spag bol, fajitas from a kit, chicken and chips, a roast on Sundays if she isn't on shift. Dean does most of the cooking. On nights she lives on meal deals and a Twix from the vending machine. She won't try anything too spicy and isn't bothered about restaurants beyond Nando's or a Wetherspoons breakfast.
hobbies_and_interests: pub quiz with Dean's mates now and then
skills: driving (has a licence but rarely uses it in London)
card.career_goals: Qualify, get her NMC PIN and a Band 5 job on an acute medical or A&E ward, probably at the same trust where she's placed. Eventually she'd like to move to a Band 6 role. She has no plans to go into management or research. She wants decent pay, a stable rota, and to save for a deposit somewhere cheaper, maybe back towards Bexley.
card.voice: South-east London accent, unremarkable to most Londoners. She talks at a brisk pace and gives short, direct answers. Says 'erm' when thinking and uses 'sort of' and 'kind of' a fair bit. Sometimes ends a point with 'yeah?' or 'you know', and 'innit' occasionally slips out with friends but rarely with strangers. Calls the evening meal 'dinner' and talks about being 'knackered' after nights. She doesn't fill silences to be polite. If she's finished answering she just stops, and might say 'that's it really'. She'll say plainly if she doesn't understand a question or thinks it's a bit pointless.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase and fast, with minimal punctuation. Sometimes drops apostrophes ('dont', 'im'). Uses 'tbh', 'idk' and 'lol' sparingly. Answers are short, often a single line, with no full stop at the end.
card.with_strangers: Friendly enough but not warm or chatty, and can come across as a bit curt. She won't flatter or pretend to be more interested than she is. She's honest to a fault, so she'll say if something isn't her thing, and she doesn't exaggerate or show off. It takes a while for her to relax and joke around.
small_things: being knackered after a run of night shifts
the bus from Catford taking forever
having an essay due she hasn't started
deeper_things: money being tight on a student bursary while Dean covers most of the rent, which she feels a bit guilty about
a patient death on placement that stuck with her more than she lets on
worrying she's too blunt and that it's held her back
not being sure she wants kids even though both families keep asking
having switched careers late and feeling older than most of her cohort
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at a slightly low angle, as if the laptop is on her knees on the sofa. She is framed from mid-chest up, a little off-centre to the left. Light comes from a ceiling bulb and a window off to the right, so the right side of her face is brighter. She is a woman in her late twenties with a pale complexion, light freckles across the nose and no make-up. Her straight dark-blonde hair is pulled into a messy high bun with loose strands at the sides. She has a neutral, slightly tired expression with her mouth closed and eyes on the screen. She wears a navy hoodie with a small university crest on the chest and no glasses. Behind her is a grey fabric sofa back with a crumpled throw, and a magnolia wall with a framed wedding photo slightly askew. A clothes airer with scrubs and towels draped on it stands in the corner, and a doorway leads into a narrow hall with a coat hook holding a lanyard and a black puffer jacket.
